title: Trim Air Zone Regulation Standard 2 with Duct-Mounted Temperature Sensing and Accumulator Damping

issue.reason: Issue C. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Second issue of the trim air regulation standard. The commanded position is now closed around a duct-mounted sensor rather than around a cabin return sensor, and an accumulator damps the pressure transients that were driving the valve to hunt.

sections.reason: The hardened seat introduced in 2016 stopped the valves failing but did not stop the cabin complaints. Analysis of eighteen months of recorded cabin data on ninety aircraft showed that the residual problem was control, not hardware: the zone loop closed around a return-air sensor with a two to three minute transport delay, so the valve hunted whenever the pack outlet moved, and on aircraft with a full cabin the aft zone overshot on every descent. Operators of the longest sectors reported that they simply left the zone selectors at the extremes, which removed any benefit from the system at all.
sections.description: The regulation standard is rebuilt around a temperature sensor mounted in the trim air duct immediately downstream of each zone valve, so that the loop closes on delivered air instead of on returned air. The valve at FIN 726HQ and the valve at FIN 980HQ are replaced by the switched assembly D2160114404059, which carries the sensor boss on the outlet flange, and the coarse filter KAD437362-51 is retained from the earlier standard. An accumulator KAE541402-61 is added upstream of each valve to damp the pressure transient that follows a pack change, and the clevis pins AES510897-5A secure its bracket to the existing duct support. A third sensing point is added at FIN 872HQ for the forward zone on ZEPHYR-24 aircraft only. The zone controller parameter set is re-scaled to the new loop gains. Work is in zones 254, 291 and 273 through the ceiling and the lateral panels. Detail is on drawings D21601147555 and D21601117401.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 3.4 kilograms per aircraft, distributed along the ceiling duct run, with no significant balance effect. Electrical load increases by 40 volt amperes for the three additional sensor channels. The standard is not interchangeable: the sensor boss is machined into the new valve outlet and the earlier valve cannot be refitted. Zone temperature overshoot on descent is reduced from an average of four degrees to less than one. The trim air maintenance tasks, the parts figure and the trouble shooting procedure for zone temperature complaints all require re-issue, and the flight crew description of the cabin temperature selection is affected because the zone now responds in under a minute.
sections.embodiment_note: Production cut-in at MSN Z08554 in September 2019. Retrofit is in two bulletins: an inspection of the duct sensor boss land, which can be done on the line, and the modification itself, which needs an overnight stop with the ceiling panels down in three zones. Kits have been available since the first quarter of 2020.

type_data.balance_impact: Distributed along the ceiling duct run, CG shift below 0.02 % MAC
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN Z08554 with a two-week duct assembly changeover
